faqs.q: How can a beginner freelancer get their first client?
faqs.a: Start by choosing a clear niche and building a small portfolio, using sample projects if you have no paid work yet. Then create a strong profile on freelancing platforms, stay active on LinkedIn and industry groups, and send short, personalised pitches to businesses you can genuinely help.

faqs.q: How much should I charge as a freelancer?
faqs.a: Base your rates on the value you deliver, your niche and the going rates for similar work, not on being the cheapest option. Very low prices tend to attract clients who haggle, while confident, clearly explained pricing that shows how you save time or earn money for a client attracts better-paying work.

faqs.q: Should freelancers do free work to win clients?
faqs.a: Offering a small piece of free value, such as a short sample, a quick website audit or a brief consultation, can build trust and show your skills. Avoid doing full projects for free; keep the free part limited so that it leads to a paid engagement rather than replacing one.

faqs.q: How do I write a pitch that gets replies from clients?
faqs.a: Keep it short, specific and about the client, not about you. Show that you understand their business and a problem they face, explain clearly how you can solve it, and include one or two relevant examples of past work. Generic copy-and-paste messages are usually ignored.
